O1.title: OLED on QWIIC
O1.heading: Turn on the SSD1306 OLED
O1.goal: Connect an SSD1306 OLED to the Pulsar C5 and show a message. This first screen experiment uses only the OLED.
steps: Unplug USB and connect the SSD1306 OLED to QWIIC, or wire only its four pins as shown.
Install Adafruit SSD1306 and Adafruit GFX Library in Arduino IDE.
Open Code to read o1-oled.ino, then upload it. The display shows Pulsar C5 and OLED ready.
O1.note: This example expects a 128 × 64 OLED at I²C address 0x3C. Change the dimensions or address in the code if your module differs. The Pulsar C5 QWIIC connector has no on-board pull-ups; most OLED modules include them.

micropython.label: MicroPython
steps: Unplug USB and connect only the SSD1306 OLED to QWIIC, or wire its four pins as shown.
Open Code, connect the serial REPL and select Install ssd1306.py. This saves the OLED driver on the board.
Run oled.py. The OLED shows Pulsar C5 and MicroPython.
micropython.note: No light sensor is needed. This example expects a 128 × 64 SSD1306 at 0x3C. If you have a 128 × 32 display, set HEIGHT to 32 in oled.py.

O2.title: ST7735 TFT
O2.heading: Draw on the 80×160 TFT
O2.goal: Connect the ST7735 to the Pulsar C5 and draw colour bars, text and shapes with MicroPython.

head: ST7735 TFT
Pulsar C5
Purpose
rows: chip select; leaves QWIIC SDA free
backlight always on; leave open if your module already connects it

steps: Unplug USB and wire the 80×160 ST7735 TFT as shown. Its SDA/SCL labels are SPI, not QWIIC.
Open Code and connect the MicroPython REPL. Install st7735.py only if the board does not already have it.
Run st7735_display.py. Look for red, green and blue screens, then text and shapes.
O2.note: CS uses D4/GPIO9 so A1/GPIO1 stays free for QWIIC SDA. Move any older TFT CS wire from A1 to D4 with USB unplugged. This example uses the green-tab 80×160 ST7735 with column offset 26 and row offset 1; the onboard microSD is kept deselected on GPIO23. If your module differs, adjust xoffset/yoffset in the example.

O3.title: TFT showcase
O3.heading: Animate the ST7735 screen
O3.goal: Use the same ST7735 wiring to show four animated MicroPython scenes, changing them with the on-board BOOT button.
steps: Keep the ST7735 wired exactly as in O2, with CS on D4/GPIO9. No extra wires are needed.
Open Code, install st7735.py if needed, then run st7735_showcase.py.
Press BOOT to switch between Bars, Orbit, Waves and System. Watch the scene name in the serial terminal.
Press Stop in the editor when you want to return to the REPL.
O3.note: Press BOOT after startup; holding it during reset enters download mode. The animation uses the TFT's own SPI pins and the on-board button on GPIO28.
